script:
This is how advanced robots learn to walk before they even exist.
If you taught a real robot through trial and error, it would constantly fall and break.
So companies like Figure and Nvidia train them inside a physics simulator.
What you're looking at is thousands of virtual robots learning at the exact same time.
They trip, slip, and fall millions of times.
And because it's running on GPUs, you can simulate years of walking data in just a few hours.
Now, the wildest part is making the jump into the real world.
Roboticists call this the sim-to-real gap.
Simulated physics is only an approximation, but real floors have random friction and motor delays.
To fix that, engineers use something called domain randomization.
Think of it like throwing constant digital curveballs.
The simulator randomizes ground friction, adds sensor noise, and even shoves the robots while they walk.
So when that AI is loaded onto a real machine, it walks on day one with zero extra tuning.
That's the big takeaway.
In just a few years, humanoid robots will show up with decades of practice before taking their very first real step.
Follow for more stories like this about tech, AI, and robotics.
